take: Coursera exposes a dedicated learner Resources branch beside Course Material modules; this suggests adjacent structures rather than demonstrated mirroring.
observed: The left navigation shows Course Material with Modules 1–4 and a separate Resources list. The selected glossary page contains an external link and a DOCX attachment.
limits: Learner side only; no matching instructor editor or same-course authoring hierarchy is retained.

take: Coursera keeps media, attachments, and sequential navigation inside one mobile lesson shell.
observed: A video sits above Transcript, Notes, Summary, and Attachments tabs, with Previous and Next controls.
limits: Shows learner consumption and sequence, not instructor/learner parity.

take: Skillshare ties project resources to lesson progression by references, while placing downloads in a separate learner tab.
observed: Projects & Resources contains project instructions that cite lesson numbers and three downloadable resource cards.
limits: No instructor view is paired; the screen cannot prove that authoring structure is mirrored.

take: Skillshare presents an ordered learner lesson list beside the player, distinct from its resource-tab organization.
observed: Ten numbered lessons with durations appear alongside the class video; Projects & Resources is a separate top-level tab.
limits: Learner side only and no same-course instructor capture.

take: This Podia capture is instructor-side evidence of resources embedded in a section, not learner-side evidence for mirroring.
observed: Done and Publish controls, editable course copy, linked resources, and a Section deleted toast are visible.
limits: Authoring-side Q2 evidence; no learner-side counterpart is retained.

take: Podia authors add a file as a lesson item inside the course section alongside links and coaching entries.
observed: The three-step flow opens New lesson > Add files, shows upload progress on a PDF row, then leaves the completed file in the section.
limits: Authoring side only; it qualifies the Q6 Podia claim but does not establish parity.

take: This Teachable capture is an instructor curriculum editor, not evidence of a learner-facing mirrored structure.
observed: Admin navigation, drag handles, Publish and Edit controls, and a Preview button surround lesson text and an Introduction.docx resource; the outline groups lessons into named sections.
limits: Misclassified for Q6; Preview is available but its learner result is not shown.

take: Teachable gives instructors an ordered section-and-lesson curriculum with item-level publication state.
observed: Named sections contain ordered lessons with content summaries, Published or Publish states, drag handles, and section-level Drip controls.
limits: Instructor side only; there is no same-course learner capture for comparison.

take: Teachable inserts PDF material inside the lesson editing context.
observed: An Add PDF dialog offers local and cloud sources plus a link option over the lesson editor.
limits: Authoring evidence only; it does not show where the PDF appears to learners.

take: SuperHi groups learner materials by content type, separating downloads from a numbered video list.
observed: The page has a Links + downloads card followed by a Videos section with lesson numbers and thumbnails.
limits: Learner-side course-adjacent evidence only; no instructor comparison is retained.
